content.text: {"predictors": [{"name": "Supplier Concentration Fragility", "construction": "From annual 10-K disclosures, count the number of major customers/suppliers a firm names (segment and customer-concentration footnotes) and compute the fraction of revenue attributable to the top customer. Rank firms by revenue-weighted customer concentration. Update annually at fiscal year end, lagged 4 months.", "rationale": "Firms dependent on a few large customers bear undiversified demand risk that is slow to be priced, and investors underappreciate the tail risk of customer loss.", "higher_returns_for": "high customer concentration"}, {"name": "Inventory-Sales Divergence", "construction": "Compute year-over-year growth in inventory (Compustat INVT) minus year-over-year growth in sales (SALE). Sort stocks cross-sectionally each month using the most recent lagged annual figures.", "rationale": "Inventory building faster than sales signals overoptimistic demand expectations and future markdowns, which the market is slow to discount.", "higher_returns_for": "low inventory-minus-sales growth"}, {"name": "Accrual Volatility", "construction": "For each firm compute total accruals (change in non-cash working capital minus depreciation, scaled by average assets) each year, then take the standard deviation of annual accruals over the trailing 5 fiscal years. Rank cross-sectionally.", "rationale": "Unstable accruals proxy for low earnings quality and information risk, commanding a return premium as investors demand compensation for opacity.", "higher_returns_for": "high accrual volatility"}, {"name": "Order Backlog Momentum", "construction": "Using the order-backlog item disclosed in 10-Ks (Compustat OB when available), compute year-over-year change in backlog scaled by total assets. Rank firms with reported backlog; update annually with a 4-month lag.", "rationale": "Growing backlog is a forward-looking signal of future revenue that is under-weighted because it sits outside standard income-statement metrics.", "higher_returns_for": "high backlog growth"}, {"name": "Dividend Initiation Recency", "construction": "Flag firms that initiated a cash dividend (first nonzero dividend after 3+ years of zero) within the trailing 12 months using CRSP distribution codes. Within dividend-initiators, sort by size of the initiated yield.", "rationale": "Dividend initiation is a costly credible signal of sustainable cash flows that the market underreacts to over subsequent quarters.", "higher_returns_for": "recent initiators with higher initiated yield"}, {"name": "R&D Acceleration", "construction": "Compute the second difference in R&D intensity: (R&D/sales in year t minus R&D/sales in year t-1) minus (R&D/sales in t-1 minus R&D/sales in t-2), using Compustat XRD and SALE. Rank cross-sectionally, treating missing R&D as zero only for R&D-reporting industries.", "rationale": "Accelerating R&D investment reflects intensifying growth options that are systematically underpriced due to conservative accounting expensing.", "higher_returns_for": "high R&D acceleration"}, {"name": "Turnover-Adjusted Illiquidity", "construction": "Compute Amihud illiquidity (mean of |daily return|/dollar volume over the year) and divide by share turnover (annual volume/shares outstanding), forming an illiquidity measure orthogonalized to trading activity. Rank monthly.", "rationale": "Isolating price-impact illiquidity from trading intensity better captures the illiquidity premium than raw measures conflated with turnover.", "higher_returns_for": "high turnover-adjusted illiquidity"}, {"name": "Capital Expenditure Smoothness", "construction": "Compute the coefficient of variation of annual capital expenditures (Compustat CAPX scaled by lagged assets) over the trailing 5 years. Rank cross-sectionally each year.", "rationale": "Lumpy, volatile investment reflects real-options exercise timing and investment risk; smooth investors face lower ex-ante risk and lower required returns.", "higher_returns_for": "high capex volatility"}, {"name": "Gross Margin Trend", "construction": "Compute the slope of a trailing 5-year regression of gross margin (GP/SALE, i.e., (SALE-COGS)/SALE) on time. Rank firms by the fitted slope, updated annually with a lag.", "rationale": "Improving margins signal strengthening competitive position and pricing power that analysts extrapolate too slowly.", "higher_returns_for": "high (positive) margin trend"}, {"name": "Financing Deficit Persistence", "construction": "For each year compute the external financing deficit (investment plus dividends minus internal cash flow, scaled by assets) and count how many of the trailing 3 years the firm ran a positive deficit requiring external funding. Rank cross-sectionally.", "rationale": "Chronically cash-hungry firms tend to issue overvalued securities and disappoint, so persistent deficit firms underperform.", "higher_returns_for": "low financing-deficit persistence"}]}
